meta.title: Seeing in the Sea 海中视觉

blocks.html:
READING PASSAGE 2

Read the passage and answer Questions 14–26.

Seeing in the Sea

Beneath the waves, ocean animals with bizarre and exotic ways of seeing create new understandings of vision

A Of all the human senses, the visual system – the network that turns light into neural signals that create the perception of sight – is the most studied and best understood. Our intense curiosity about sight is no coincidence: we are animals who judge the world mostly by appearances rather than, say, by aromas. But our eyes allow us only one view out of a multitude of possibilities. In the depths of the ocean – a world we are beginning to learn about in detail – marine species have developed visual systems drastically different from our own. The majority of eyes, whether on land or in the sea, share two basic components: something to focus light as it hits the eye (for humans, a cornea and lens), and something to absorb and detect the light (a retina). Then the divergences begin.

B Ocean creatures’ eyes have evolved a bewildering array of structures suited to each animal’s place in the natural order and the depth at which it lives. Some amphipods (deep-sea crustaceans) rely on biological fiber-optic cables to send light to their retina. Sight-dependent, nomadic predators have excellent vision, whereas many creatures that live at great depths can make only simple distinctions between light and dark. Light is abundant in the sunny shallows, but 50 feet below the surface, only the shorter wavelengths are able to penetrate, eliminating all discernable colors except blue. By about one mile down, the last traces of sunlight disappear. In this realm of perpetual night, the only illumination is manufactured, provided by the many creatures that generate their own light in a process known as bioluminescence.

C As they search for prey, swordfish swim through cold, deep water, occasionally diving as far as 3,000 feet below the surface. But even in the chilly depths, the swordfish keeps its eyes and brain 10 to 15 degrees Celsius warmer than the surrounding water by means of an unusual heat-generating muscle near the fish’s eye. Vision researcher Kerstin Fritsches, of the University of Queensland in Australia, along with colleagues there and in the United States and Sweden, found that keeping warm improves the swordfish’s vision. At 20°C, the scientists found, a swordfish retina can detect objects moving five times as quickly as the objects it can spot at 10°C. Since swordfish hunt speedy prey like squid, the ability to see fast-moving swimmers is crucial for finding dinner.

D The box jellyfish has surprisingly sophisticated eyes. It possesses a total of 24, divided among four eyestalks at the corners of its body. Four of the eyes on each stalk are simply groups of light-sensing cells that help it distinguish between bright and dark. The other two are complex, with lenses that produce high-quality images – but those lenses focus light well below the retina, meaning that the images are out of focus when they hit the light receptors. ‘They’re not really interested in fine details,’ says biologist Dan Nilsson, of the University of Lund in Sweden. Once the jellyfish can see the outlines of its environment, signals from its four simple brains (one in each eyestalk) steer it home to the shallow coastal waters of Australia, all the way from Puerto Rico on the other side of the world.

E The mantis shrimp, an inhabitant of tropical waters, leads a particularly vibrant life. University of Queensland neurobiologist Justin Marshall found that this crustacean has 12 different color receptors – cells in the retina that are sensitive to different wavelengths of light – whereas humans have only three. These shrimp behold a world we cannot begin to imagine: in addition to seeing a much richer light spectrum, they perceive linear and circular polarized light. Marshall suspects the ability to see polarized light ‘probably has something to do with reproduction’. A flash of polarized light reflected off a female shrimp, for example, could catch the eye of a potential mate without drawing unwanted attention from predators.

F In the deep-sea darkness, beyond the reach of the sun’s rays, some creatures make their own light. Organically created light, or bioluminescence, is so useful that it has evolved independently about 40 times across a range of creatures during the course of life on Earth, says bioluminescence expert Edith Widder, founder and CEO of the Ocean Research and Conservation Association in Fort Pierce, Florida, in the United States. Female anglerfish let someone else do the work, relying on colonies of light-emitting bacteria to give their lure its distinctive glow. The visual systems of male anglerfish are attuned to this light source; they can tell whether a female belongs to their species just by the silhouette of her lure, thus making it easy to find a mate in the dark.

G The atolla jellyfish, found in oceans across the globe, is high on beauty but low on brains. Looking beyond the scarlet tentacles will reveal that the creature has no central nervous system. Since it lacks the neural architecture to interpret complex visual information, the jellyfish must rely on its simple but numerous pigment cups. When attacked, as part of its defence the atolla launches a stunning blue bioluminescent display visible for hundreds of feet through the dusky mid-depth waters where it lives. Blue hues are the only colors of light able to penetrate that far below the surface, so the atolla’s red pigmentation normally makes it largely invisible.

questionGroups.bodyHtml:
Questions 14–19

The text has seven paragraphs, A–G. Which paragraph contains the following information? You may choose any paragraph more than once.

Paragraphs

14 an example of an ocean animal which can see colour differently from humans

15 a simple description of how most eyes work

16 a reference to the frequency with which one biological trait has developed in different species

17 a description of a sea creature which travels huge distances

18 details of a creature that protects itself by means of light

19 a description of a creature with multiple eyes

A. Paragraph A
B. Paragraph B
C. Paragraph C
D. Paragraph D
E. Paragraph E
F. Paragraph F
G. Paragraph G

Questions 20 and 21

Choose TWO correct answers.

In which TWO of the following sea creatures does one gender attract the other using light?

Questions 22–26

Complete the summary. Write ONE WORD AND/OR A NUMBER from the text for each answer.

How the eyes of ocean creatures have developed differently from those of land creatures

22 Ocean creatures' eyes have developed many different according to the depth of the water where they live. Ocean roaming predators have well developed eyesight because they hunt where there is plenty of light. However, light only reaches the of some sea creatures of the deep via fibre-optic cables, and by 50 feet deep, is the only colour which is visible. At a depth of around , no light from the sun can get through. At this level, the only source of light is that which is produced through .

items.text:
题目翻译：一个海洋动物的色觉与人类不同的例子。
答案：E
解析：E段将螳螂虾的12种颜色受体与人类的三种直接对比，并说它们能看到丰富得多的光谱，正对应 see colour differently from humans，所以选 E。B段讨论的是不同水深的光线变化，没有比较某种动物与人类的色觉。
定位：正文 E 段
University of Queensland neurobiologist Justin Marshall found that this crustacean has 12 different color receptors – cells in the retina that are sensitive to different wavelengths of light – whereas humans have only three. These shrimp behold a world we cannot begin to imagine: in addition to seeing a much richer light spectrum, they perceive linear and circular polarized light.
原文翻译：昆士兰大学的神经生物学家 Justin Marshall 发现，这种甲壳类动物有12种不同的颜色受体——即视网膜中对不同波长的光敏感的细胞——而人类只有三种。这些虾看到的世界，是我们根本无法想象的：除了能看见丰富得多的光谱，它们还能感知线偏振光和圆偏振光。

题目翻译：对大多数眼睛如何工作的简要说明。
答案：A
解析：A段先说 The majority of eyes（大多数眼睛），再概括聚焦光线、吸收并感知光线这两个基本环节，正好说明 most eyes 如何工作，所以选 A。
定位：正文 A 段
The majority of eyes, whether on land or in the sea, share two basic components: something to focus light as it hits the eye (for humans, a cornea and lens), and something to absorb and detect the light (a retina). Then the divergences begin.
原文翻译：无论是在陆地上还是海洋中，大多数眼睛都有两个基本组成部分：一部分在光进入眼睛时将其聚焦（在人类身上，是角膜和晶状体），另一部分则吸收并感知光（即视网膜）。从这里开始，各种眼睛便出现了差异。

题目翻译：提到某一生物特征在不同物种中演化出现的次数。
答案：F
解析：F段说，生物发光在多种生物中独立演化了大约40次。about 40 times 对应题干的 frequency，across a range of creatures 对应不同物种，所以选 F。这里问的是演化出现的次数，不是单只动物发光的频率。
定位：正文 F 段
Organically created light, or bioluminescence, is so useful that it has evolved independently about 40 times across a range of creatures during the course of life on Earth, says bioluminescence expert Edith Widder, founder and CEO of the Ocean Research and Conservation Association in Fort Pierce, Florida, in the United States.
原文翻译：生物发光专家 Edith Widder 说，生物自身产生的光，也就是生物发光，用途如此之大，以至于在地球生命演化的过程中，它在多种生物中独立演化了大约40次；Widder 是海洋研究与保护协会（Ocean Research and Conservation Association）的创始人兼首席执行官，该协会位于美国佛罗里达州皮尔斯堡（Fort Pierce）。

题目翻译：对一种会移动极远距离的海洋生物的描述。
答案：D
解析：D段末句描述箱形水母从地球另一端的 Puerto Rico 一路返回澳大利亚沿岸浅水区。这段跨越极远距离的描述对应 travels huge distances，因此选 D。题干没有要求季节性迁徙，不能额外加入这一条件。
定位：正文 D 段
Once the jellyfish can see the outlines of its environment, signals from its four simple brains (one in each eyestalk) steer it home to the shallow coastal waters of Australia, all the way from Puerto Rico on the other side of the world.
原文翻译：一旦水母看清周围环境的轮廓，它的四个简单大脑（每个眼柄中有一个）就会发出信号，引导它一路从地球另一端的波多黎各（Puerto Rico），回到澳大利亚沿岸的浅水区。

题目翻译：关于一种利用光保护自己的生物的详细说明。
答案：G
解析：G段说 atolla 水母在遭到攻击时发出蓝色生物光，并明确写出 as part of its defence，说明这是保护自己的手段，所以选 G。F段鮟鱇的发光在这里用于寻找配偶，目的不同。
定位：正文 G 段
When attacked, as part of its defence the atolla launches a stunning blue bioluminescent display visible for hundreds of feet through the dusky mid-depth waters where it lives.
原文翻译：遭到攻击时，atolla 水母会发出一片令人惊叹的蓝色生物光，作为防御手段的一部分；在它生活的昏暗中层水域中，数百英尺之外也能看到。

题目翻译：对一种拥有多只眼睛的生物的描述。
答案：D
解析：D段开头说箱形水母共有24只眼睛，分布在四个眼柄上，直接对应 multiple eyes，因此选 D。题目允许重复使用段落字母，所以它可以与另一道关于远距离移动的题选择同一段。
定位：正文 D 段
The box jellyfish has surprisingly sophisticated eyes. It possesses a total of 24, divided among four eyestalks at the corners of its body.
原文翻译：箱形水母（box jellyfish）的眼睛复杂得出人意料。它共有24只眼睛，分布在身体四角的四个眼柄上。

items.text:
题目翻译：以下哪两种海洋生物中，一种性别会利用光吸引另一种性别？
答案：C
解析：E段说雌性螳螂虾反射的偏振光，可能吸引潜在配偶的注意；F段则说雄性鮟鱇能借雌性的发光诱饵在黑暗中找到配偶。因此两项是 C 和 D，顺序不限。A 剑鱼的保温机制有助于看清快速猎物；B 箱形水母的视觉用于辨别环境、引导行动；E atolla 水母的发光用于防御，它们在文中都不是利用光吸引异性的例子。
定位：正文 E 段
Marshall suspects the ability to see polarized light ‘probably has something to do with reproduction’. A flash of polarized light reflected off a female shrimp, for example, could catch the eye of a potential mate without drawing unwanted attention from predators.
原文翻译：Marshall 推测，看见偏振光的能力“很可能与繁殖有关”。例如，雌虾身上反射出的一闪而过的偏振光，可能吸引潜在配偶的注意，同时又不引起捕食者的注意。

The visual systems of male anglerfish are attuned to this light source; they can tell whether a female belongs to their species just by the silhouette of her lure, thus making it easy to find a mate in the dark.
原文翻译：雌性鮟鱇（anglerfish）让别的生物代劳，依靠一群群发光细菌，使自己的诱饵发出独特的光。雄性鮟鱇的视觉系统与这种光源相适应；仅凭雌性诱饵的轮廓，它们就能判断对方是否属于同一物种，因此很容易在黑暗中找到配偶。

items.text:
题目翻译：海洋生物的眼睛根据其生活水深，演化出了许多不同的______。
答案：structures
解析：B段开头的 evolved a bewildering array of structures 对应题干 developed many different，后面又说明这些结构与生活水深相适应，所以填 structures。many different 后需要可数名词复数，保留原文词形。
定位：正文 B 段
Ocean creatures’ eyes have evolved a bewildering array of structures suited to each animal’s place in the natural order and the depth at which it lives.
原文翻译：海洋生物的眼睛演化出了形形色色的结构，以适应各自的生态位置和生活水深。

题目翻译：光只能通过光纤，到达一些深海生物的______。
答案：retina
解析：原文说生物光纤将光 send ... to their retina，题干改成光经由光纤到达某个部位，因此填 retina（视网膜）。原句使用单数 retina；their 并不要求后面的身体部位一定用复数。
定位：正文 B 段
Some amphipods (deep-sea crustaceans) rely on biological fiber-optic cables to send light to their retina.
原文翻译：一些端足类动物（amphipods，深海甲壳类动物）依靠生物光纤将光传送到视网膜。

题目翻译：在50英尺深处，唯一可见的颜色是______。
答案：blue
解析：原文说水下50英尺处，all discernable colors except blue 都消失了，也就是只有蓝色可见，对应题干 the only colour，填 blue。不要与后面完全没有阳光的一英里深处混淆。
定位：正文 B 段
Light is abundant in the sunny shallows, but 50 feet below the surface, only the shorter wavelengths are able to penetrate, eliminating all discernable colors except blue.
原文翻译：阳光照耀的浅水区光线充足，但到了水面下50英尺，只有波长较短的光能够穿透，除蓝色外，其他可辨别的颜色都消失了。

题目翻译：在约______的深度，阳光已无法穿透。
答案：one mile
可接受答案：one mile / 1 mile
解析：原文 By about one mile down, the last traces of sunlight disappear 对应题干 At a depth of around ... no light from the sun can get through。空后没有预印单位，所以填 1 mile，数字加一个词，符合题目限制；只填 1 或 mile 都不完整。原文的 one mile 与 1 mile 数值、单位完全相同。
定位：正文 B 段
By about one mile down, the last traces of sunlight disappear.
原文翻译：到了约一英里深的地方，最后一丝阳光也消失了。

题目翻译：在这一深度，唯一的光源是通过______产生的光。
答案：bioluminescence
解析：题干说，这一深度的唯一光源由某个过程产生。原文把生物自行发光的过程称为 bioluminescence，produced through 对应 in a process known as，因此填 bioluminescence（生物发光）。
定位：正文 B 段
In this realm of perpetual night, the only illumination is manufactured, provided by the many creatures that generate their own light in a process known as bioluminescence.
原文翻译：在这片永夜世界里，唯一的照明来自生物自己制造的光：许多生物通过一种名为“生物发光”的过程，产生自身的光。

questionExplanations.text:
题目翻译：海洋生物的眼睛根据其生活水深，演化出了许多不同的______。
答案：structures
解析：B段开头的 evolved a bewildering array of structures 对应题干 developed many different，后面又说明这些结构与生活水深相适应，所以填 structures。many different 后需要可数名词复数，保留原文词形。
定位：正文 B 段
Ocean creatures’ eyes have evolved a bewildering array of structures suited to each animal’s place in the natural order and the depth at which it lives.
原文翻译：海洋生物的眼睛演化出了形形色色的结构，以适应各自的生态位置和生活水深。

题目翻译：光只能通过光纤，到达一些深海生物的______。
答案：retina
解析：原文说生物光纤将光 send ... to their retina，题干改成光经由光纤到达某个部位，因此填 retina（视网膜）。原句使用单数 retina；their 并不要求后面的身体部位一定用复数。
定位：正文 B 段
Some amphipods (deep-sea crustaceans) rely on biological fiber-optic cables to send light to their retina.
原文翻译：一些端足类动物（amphipods，深海甲壳类动物）依靠生物光纤将光传送到视网膜。
